summary: The CSA Cyber Trust mark (SS 712) certifies that an organisation manages cyber risk in proportion to its exposure. It uses five preparedness tiers and four pillars, is valid for three years with yearly audits, and is issued by CSA-appointed certification bodies. ICFC helps you choose the right tier, prepare, and train your team.
what: The Cyber Trust mark is CSA's risk-based cybersecurity certification for organisations with more extensive digital operations. The 2025 edition is published as Singapore Standard SS 712 and now covers classical IT, cloud, operational technology (OT) and AI security.
who: Organisations that handle sensitive data, serve enterprise or government buyers, or rely heavily on digital systems, cloud or OT.
keywords: Cyber Trust mark Singapore, SS 712, CSA certification, cybersecurity tiers
edgeNote: This mark is funded by CSA rather than EDGE. CSA funds the first successful certification only, for SMEs and non-profit organisations incorporated in Singapore, until 6 February 2028. The amount is deducted from the fee charged by the CSA-appointed certification body. Consultancy fees are not covered by this funding.

extra.heading: Tiers
extra.text: Five cybersecurity preparedness tiers: Supporter, Practitioner, Promoter, Performer and Advocate. CSA's risk assessment framework points each organisation to its tier, and each tier carries between 10 and 22 preparedness domains. The tier reflects how much cyber risk the business carries, not its size.

extra.heading: Pillars
extra.text: Classical cybersecurity is the base pillar. Cloud security, operational technology (OT) security and AI security are added as pillars where they apply to your operations.

extra.heading: CSA funding (Cyber Trust 2025)
extra.text: For the classical pillar, CSA's maximum support ranges from S$1,375 (1 to 10 end-points) to S$2,250 (101 to 200 end-points). Each added cloud, OT or AI pillar attracts S$225, or S$450 for 101 to 200 end-points, giving up to S$3,600 in total. First certification only, for Singapore-incorporated SMEs and non-profits, until 6 February 2028. Figures from CSA, checked 11 October 2026.

impartiality.heading: Primary principle
impartiality.text: Impartiality comes first. Every engagement begins with a conflict-of-interest check. We keep consulting and auditing roles separate, and our auditors never audit, on behalf of a certification body, an organisation that ICFC has consulted on the same scope within the period set by that body.

faqs.q: Which Cyber Trust tier do we need?
faqs.a: Your tier comes from CSA's risk assessment template. We run it with you, explain the result, and plan the controls for that tier only, so you do not over-build.

faqs.q: Is Cyber Trust the same as ISO/IEC 27001?
faqs.a: No. Both are risk-based, and CSA publishes a mapping between them, but they are separate certifications. Organisations certified to one can reuse much of the evidence for the other.

faqs.q: How long is the certificate valid?
faqs.a: Three years, with an audit each year to keep it active.

faqs.q: Can we start with Cyber Essentials instead?
faqs.a: Yes. Cyber Essentials suits organisations at the start of their journey and is a natural stepping stone to Cyber Trust.
